title: Both readings are early; the grammar favours the person

points.label: The person purifies
points.text: Qatada: whoever **purifies himself by righteous deeds**; Mujahid, ʿIkrima and Saʿid ibn Jubayr: “whoever sets it right”. The simplest grammar makes **man** (“whoever”) the subject of the verb zakkā.
points.who: Qatada, Mujahid, ʿIkrima, Saʿid ibn Jubayr

points.label: God purifies
points.text: Ibn ʿAbbas (via ʿAli ibn Abi Talha and al-ʿAwfi) and Ibn Zayd: successful is the one **whose soul God purifies**. Al-Tabari’s own gloss opens this way. It continues verse 8, where **God is the actor**.
points.who: Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Zayd; al-Tabari’s gloss

points.label: A prayer that joins them
points.text: Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet’s prayer (Muslim, via Zayd ibn Arqam): “Give my soul its **taqwā** and purify it; **You are the best of those who purify it**.” It echoes verses 8–9.

bottom_text: No consensus: Ibn Kathir gives both without ranking them. The wording leans to the human as subject; the God reading needs an unstated subject but fits verse 8’s flow.
